title: Quotations for Chapter 22 (Marx: accumulation, crisis and the schemes of reproduction): Capital, vols. 1-3 (1867, 1885, 1894; the English of 1887 and 1909), the preface of Zur Kritik (1859); D. M. Evans on the crisis of 1857 and the report of the Select Committee on the Bank Acts (1858); M. Wirth on Hamburg in 1857 (1858); Tugan-Baranowsky (1901), Böhm-Bawerk (1896), Hilferding's reply (1904), Luxemburg (1913), Kalecki (1954); Allen's 'Engels' pause' (2009); Nakatani and Hagiwara on the Okishio theorem (1997); the Nobel press release of 1973 and Leontief's autobiography; the Dictionary of National Biography on Evans (1889)
source: K. Marx, Das Kapital I (Hamburg 1867), II (1885), III (1894), Zur Kritik der politischen Oekonomie (Berlin 1859); Capital, vol. II of the English edition of 1887 (Moore and Aveling); Capital, vols. II and III, tr. E. Untermann (Chicago: Kerr, 1909); D. M. Evans, The History of the Commercial Crisis, 1857-58 (London 1859); M. Wirth, Geschichte der Handelskrisen (Frankfurt 1858); M. v. Tugan-Baranowsky, Studien zur Theorie und Geschichte der Handelskrisen in England (Jena 1901); E. v. Böhm-Bawerk, Zum Abschluss des Marxschen Systems (Berlin 1896); R. Hilferding, Böhm-Bawerks Marx-Kritik (Wien 1904; Marxists Internet Archive); R. Luxemburg, Die Akkumulation des Kapitals (Berlin 1913); M. Kalecki, Theory of Economic Dynamics (London 1954); R. C. Allen, Explorations in Economic History 46 (2009), article in press; T. Nakatani and T. Hagiwara, Kobe University Economic Review 43 (1997); nobelprize.org (1973; press release and autobiography); A. R. V[ian], 'Evans, David Morier', Dictionary of National Biography 18 (1889)
series: id, dynasty (place), year, year_note, value (numbers in the quotation, ';'-separated; 'a+b/c' for a mixed fraction), unit, numeral (unused), file (key of 'sources'), juan (location: chapter, printed page), quote (verbatim, as in the document's text, OCR misreadings included; for a scheme, the printed line), note
license: Quotations for criticism and teaching, each with its source. Marx (1859, 1867, 1885, 1894), the English translation of 1887, Evans (1859), Wirth (1858), Tugan-Baranowsky (1901), Böhm-Bawerk (1896), Hilferding (1904; the author died in 1941), Luxemburg (1913) and the Dictionary of National Biography (1889; transcribed on Wikisource) are in the public domain; the archive.org texts are OCR of public-domain scans (Wirth: a Google Books scan, whose usage guidelines ask that the files be used for non-commercial purposes). Untermann's translation of Capital, vols. II and III (Kerr, 1909), is in the public domain in the United States, where it was published; it is quoted only for the printed lines of the schemes and a few short sentences. Kalecki (1954): 'This book is copyright under the Berne Convention'; only short phrases (a formula and parts of three sentences) are quoted. Allen (2009): '© 2009 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.'; short passages (a sentence or part of one) with full credit. Nakatani and Hagiwara (1997), Kobe University Repository: Kernel: short passages with full credit. The nobelprize.org pages ('Copyright © Nobel Prize Outreach 2026'; the autobiography: 'Copyright © The Nobel Foundation 1973') are quoted, not copied. The chapter's Chinese renders the German and English; the translations are the book's.
fetch: data/fetch/verify_web_quotes.py (every row whose file is a key of 'sources', except the two page images marx1894de_p191 and marx1909k3_p247, which were read by eye); checks/check_ch22.py (the readings and every quotation of the text)
notes: The schemes of reproduction are quoted from Untermann's English (Kerr), because the OCR of the German first edition loses the subscripts and fractions of the scheme lines; the German is quoted for Marx's words. Marx's printed numbers contain slips, kept as printed: in the expanded scheme the aggregate capital at the start is printed '5400 c + 1750 v = 7150' for 5500 c + 1750 v = 7250 (row k2_7150), and the product of department II in the fourth year '4249' where the rule of the scheme gives 4259.2 and the three terms he prints, 2129 + 1065 + 1065, add up to 4259 (row k2_B4); the table of vol. III, chapter 13 prints a profit rate of '66⅓%' for c = 50, v = 100, m = 100, where 100/150 = 66⅔% (rows k3_tab_50, k3en_tab_50; the German first edition and Kerr's translation print the same). Evans gives two dates for the rise of Bank Rate to 10 per cent in November 1857 (11 November in his narrative, row ev_rate10; 9 November in the speech of row ev_rates_commons); the Bank of England's table D1 gives 12 November (snapshot boe_millennium_bank_rate_1856_1858). Evans's 'Select Committee' paragraphs are from the report of the Select Committee on the Bank Acts of 1858, which Evans reprints; the committee quotes 'our Consul' at Hamburg without naming him. Wirth's OCR (Fraktur, Google scan) misreads many letters: the rows keep the OCR, and the note gives the reading. The Fraktur OCR of Luxemburg keeps the double hyphen (⸗) at line ends, which verify_web_quotes.py does not join, so the rows keep it. Luxemburg's p. 340 has no page header in the OCR (between pp. 339 and 341). The Tugan page headers 26 and 27 are missing in the OCR; rows tu_purpose (p. 26) and tu_synthesis, tu_kernel (note 1 on p. 27) are placed by the headers on either side. The PDF texts are searched in pdftotext's normal and -layout output. Rows added by the editor after the review (2026-10-16), each found verbatim in the cached document: k3_sum, k3_market, k3_costprice, k3_notnow (vol. III, ch. 9, on the transformation), hi_* (Hilferding's reply to Böhm-Bawerk), lu_ground and lu_end (the rest of Luxemburg's sentence on imperialism), tu_surplus (the sentence before tu_sismondi), al_expected and al_mediate (Allen pp. 12-13), and the Hamburg rows wi_nov27, wi_second, wi_sola, wi_pledge, wi_cash, wi_twoweeks and wi_dec15 (Wirth's second measure of 27 November).
